analysis.title: Economics Weekly: Housing's Long Winter
key_insights: Mortgage rates averaged 7.33% in October, the highest monthly level since late 2023, and eased only to 7.11% by mid-November. The 30-year rate has risen every month since February's 6.05% average. The MBA purchase index is down about 20% from its early-February high.
Existing home sales fell 5.5% in October to a 3.75 million annual rate, the lowest since August 2010. Pending sales hit a record low, which points to more weakness ahead.

Affordability is the binding constraint. The monthly payment on the median existing home is up about 12% year on year and higher rates explain almost all of it. NAHB estimates 65% of households cannot afford the median new home even at 6%, and about 70% at October's rate.

Lock-in persists. The average outstanding mortgage rate is 4.4%, about 2.7 points below the current 30-year rate, and nearly half of borrowers hold loans below 4%. The share of mortgages at 6% or higher may pass 25% by mid-2027 from 23% in Q2.

William Blair expects the Fed to hike 25bp in December and again early next year. It sees the 10-year Treasury yield holding at 5.00%-5.25%, so mortgage rates stay near 7% with little chance of a return to 6%. Fannie and Freddie MBS purchases of about $51B are well short of the $200B directed.

Builders are adjusting through price and incentives. New home sales were 676,000 in September, new-home supply is 8.4 months versus 5.1 months for existing homes, and 46% of builders cut prices and 68% offered incentives in November, both post-COVID highs. The median new-home price fell 3.9% year on year in September.

Construction is slowing. Housing starts averaged a 1.30 million rate over six months to October, the slowest since September 2020. Land costs, labor shortages from immigration enforcement and tighter construction and multifamily lending constrain builders. Multifamily CMBS delinquencies are 8.09%.

Existing home prices were up only 0.4% year on year in October, down from 2.6% in July. The report expects flat to lower nominal prices, and prices likely fall further only if layoffs force sales. Residential mortgage delinquencies are 1.86% in 2Q26, below the 2.3% long-term median.

Rents should firm modestly through 2027 and shelter inflation should stop easing. Rental vacancy is 7.6%, the highest since 2014, but apartment completions are back near 2019 levels and Zillow new-lease rents are up 2.9% year on year. CoStar raised its Q4 2027 rent growth forecast to 2.6% from 1.9%. The main risk is weak renter household growth.

AI investment cuts both ways for housing. A gradual slowdown in the buildout would ease long rates and labor costs. A sharp correction would also lower rates but would hit stock-market wealth and could cause job losses and forced sales.

Corporate commentary is consistent. Lennar says almost 50% of visitors cannot qualify immediately. Mohawk calls this the most challenging environment across its end-markets. UDR expects rent growth to accelerate in 2027.
The scorecard and sector tables show equities sold off in the past week, with the S&P 500 down 5.49% and semiconductors down 10.91%. Year to date the S&P 500 is up 4.83%.

sector_views.rationale: Volumes are weak, builders are trading margin for volume, and suppliers like Mohawk see soft remodeling and new construction.
New supply is falling, high ownership costs keep buyers renting, and market rents have begun to firm into 2027.

earnings_insights: Mohawk management says residential repair and remodel is about half of US sales and new construction about one-fourth, and expects the current environment to persist near term.
D.R. Horton reported stick-and-brick costs down 4% and lot costs up 6% in its latest fiscal year.
The William Blair Quarterly Analyst Survey for Q3 2026 shows a composite index of 74.1, up from 70.2.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Rates are well above the 6% level needed to restart the housing cycle.
The lowest since August 2010, so the resale market is nearly seized.

macro_indicators.reading: 1.30 million average annual rate over six months
macro_indicators.interpretation: Slowest since September 2020, and supply is tightening.

macro_indicators.reading: 25bp hike in December and another early next year
macro_indicators.interpretation: Housing weakness alone is unlikely to stop the Fed, since long rates matter most.
Yields anchored until inflation shows a sustained decline, keeping mortgage rates near 7%.
Shelter inflation is expected to stop easing as market rents firm.
The slowest since May 2021, which limits affordability support.

risk_factors: Weak renter household growth could keep rents flat despite supply normalizing.
Rising layoffs could force home sales and push prices down.
A sharp AI buildout correction would cut equity wealth that supports buyers.
Further Fed hikes and persistently high 10-year yields keep mortgage rates elevated.
Tightening credit for construction and multifamily and rising CMBS delinquencies.
charts_described: Exhibit 1 plots the mortgage rate against MBA purchase applications on an inverse scale, with purchase demand falling about 20% from its early-February high.
Exhibit 2 shows homeownership rates by age, with under-35 at 36.6% in Q3 versus 39.3% in Q3 2022.
Exhibit 4 shows single-family units under construction at 581,000, near the 1970-2015 median, and multifamily at 674,000, roughly double the norm.
geopolitical: Energy shock from the war boosted inflation this year. An end to the war could lower energy prices, but the report does not expect that quickly.
Stepped-up immigration enforcement is tightening construction labor and reducing renter household growth.

tension_points.bull_case: Apartment completions are back near 2019 pace, ownership costs keep buyers renting, and Zillow new-lease rents are up 2.9%, so rents and shelter inflation should firm through 2027.
tension_points.bear_case: Renter household growth slowed to about 336,000 and vacancy is 7.6%, which could keep rents flat even as supply normalizes.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Renter household growth stays this weak and vacancies keep rising.

tension_points.bull_case: Few owners are forced to sell and delinquencies are below the long-term median, so prices hold flat nominally.
tension_points.bear_case: Prices have historically fallen after volumes once job losses force owners to sell.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A rise in job losses leading to forced sales.

theme_stances.key_argument: Mortgage rates above 7% and affordability pressure keep sales low, and rates are unlikely to return to 6% until inflation falls.
theme_stances.evidence: Until then, we continue to curb our enthusiasm.

theme_stances.key_argument: Supply is normalizing and high ownership costs keep buyers renting, so rents and shelter inflation should firm through 2027.
theme_stances.evidence: We expect rents to firm modestly through 2027
